title: KV Cache Health Dashboard — Mockups, Panels, Alerts, and “Bad Pattern” Examples (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
KV Cache Health Dashboard
Mockups, panel definitions, and alert proposals

Owner: Allison Grant (Observability standards + alerting)
Primary users: Runtime oncall, SRE oncall, perf-canary owner, Serving Runtime engineers
Last updated: 2025-03-03

Speaker notes:
- This deck is meant to align Runtime + SRE on what we will ship for compaction rollout and ongoing ops.
- Focus is “KV cache health” signals that predict and explain tail latency spikes and OOM risk.


Slide 2 — Why we need a dedicated KV cache dashboard
Observed production issues:
- Bursty traffic + mixed sequence lengths → KV cache fragmentation → allocator churn → p95/p99 spikes
- Fragmentation also increases risk of allocation failure / near-OOM behavior → conservative admission control → throughput loss

Goals for this dashboard:
- Detect early: fragmentation trending up before p99 explodes
- Attribute: prove when tails are “KV allocator/compaction” vs “scheduler/backpressure” vs “model”
- Make canary safe: clear rollback triggers for compaction flag and budgets

Speaker notes:
- We should not ask oncall to infer fragmentation from generic GPU memory charts.
- We need per-pool/per-region breakdown and link to request latency.


Slide 3 — Audience + primary workflows
Audience:
- SRE oncall: triage + mitigation (routing/pool changes, runtime flags)
- Runtime oncall: debugging (allocator behavior, compaction overhead, races)
- Perf/Release: gate compaction rollouts

Top workflows:
1) “Tail latency regression” page → is fragmentation involved?
2) “OOM / allocation failure” page → is this true memory pressure or fragmentation?
3) Canary enablement checklist → watch dashboard for 1h/24h trend
4) Post-incident analysis → correlate events with compaction/eviction

Speaker notes:
- This is not a one-off launch dashboard; it’s a permanent operating surface.


Slide 4 — Dashboard layout (proposed)
Row A: Overview (SLO-facing)
- p95/p99 latency (decode + end-to-end)
- timeouts / 5xx rate
- throughput (req/s, tokens/s)

Row B: KV health core signals
- fragmentation ratio
- allocation failure rate
- eviction rate
- compaction activity + budget utilization

Row C: Attribution / correlation helpers
- latency with compaction events overlay
- scheduler “cache pressure” + backpressure signals
- GPU memory used vs free (KV vs non-KV if available)

Row D: Drilldowns
- by pool / region / model family
- top offending tenants (Dedicated) or top routes (Hosted)

Speaker notes:
- Top row is what leadership / paging sees.
- Middle rows are what tells you if it’s the KV subsystem.


Slide 5 — Required dimensions (filters)
Global filters:
- env: prod | staging
- region: us-east | us-west | eu-central | …
- pool: hosted-shared-X | dedicated-<acct>-Y
- model_family: llama3 | mixtral | qwen | …
- runtime_version
- compaction_enabled: true|false

Optional filters (when available):
- tenant_tier: free|pro|enterprise
- request_class: interactive|batch
- sequence_len_bucket: short|mid|long

Speaker notes:
- Drilldowns must keep cardinality manageable; we’ll do “top N” tables for route/tenant.


Slide 6 — Metric naming (draft) and definitions
NOTE: names below reflect “preferred schema”; final names may differ in telemetry pipeline.

Core KV metrics:
- runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio (gauge, 0–1)
  Definition: (unusable_free_bytes / total_free_bytes) or equivalent allocator-level fragmentation metric. We need to standardize.
- runtime_kv_alloc_failures_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_alloc_attempts_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_evictions_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_evicted_bytes_total (counter)

Compaction metrics (only when enabled):
- runtime_kv_compaction_runs_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_compaction_budget_ms (gauge)
- runtime_kv_compaction_budget_utilization_ratio (gauge, 0–1)

Latency correlation helpers:
- runtime_request_latency_ms{phase=prefill|decode|end_to_end} (histogram)
- runtime_scheduler_cache_pressure (gauge)

Speaker notes:
- For dashboards, we care more about consistent definition than perfect theoretical purity.
- Fragmentation ratio MUST be stable across versions; if definition changes, we need a version label.


Slide 7 — Panel mockup #1: “KV Cache Health — Overview”
Panel: Fragmentation ratio over time (line)
- Y: runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio
- X: time
- Split: pool (top 5 by traffic) OR selected pool
- Annotate: compaction_enabled toggle events

Panel: Allocation failure rate (line)
- (increase(runtime_kv_alloc_failures_total[5m]) / increase(runtime_kv_alloc_attempts_total[5m]))

Panel: Eviction rate (line)
- increase(runtime_kv_evictions_total[5m])

Panel: Compaction activity (stacked)
- compaction runs / bytes moved

Speaker notes:
- This is the first stop for “is KV subsystem unhealthy?”
- Annotating config changes is non-negotiable for canary.


Slide 8 — Panel mockup #2: “Latency correlation — compaction + fragmentation”
Panel: p99 decode latency with overlays
- runtime_request_latency_ms{phase=decode,quantile=0.99}
- Overlay 1: runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio (secondary axis)
- Overlay 2: compaction runs (bar)

Panel: p95 end-to-end latency
- runtime_request_latency_ms{phase=end_to_end,quantile=0.95}

Panel: Timeouts / errors
- gateway_timeouts_total or route_timeout_rate

Speaker notes:
- This panel should tell oncall: tails follow fragmentation (allocator churn) vs tails follow compaction thrash vs tails follow scheduler pressure.


Slide 9 — Panel mockup #3: “Compaction budget + safety”
Panel: Budget utilization ratio (line)
- runtime_kv_compaction_budget_utilization_ratio

Panel: Median latency guardrail (line)
- runtime_request_latency_ms{phase=decode,quantile=0.50}

Panel: Compaction time per moved GiB (derived)
- (rate(runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total[5m]) / rate(runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total[5m]))

Panel: “Compaction on allocation failure” count
- increase(runtime_kv_compaction_runs_total{trigger=alloc_failure}[10m])

Speaker notes:
- We need a quick way to detect “compaction is doing too much work” and harming median latency.
- The “time per moved GiB” is a proxy for sync overhead / bad kernel interaction.


Slide 10 — Panel mockup #4: “Eviction + fairness indicators”
Panel: Evictions by priority/tier (stacked)
- runtime_kv_evictions_total{victim_class=…}
  victim_class examples: best_effort | default | latency_sensitive | pinned

Panel: Requests impacted by eviction (if available)
- runtime_kv_eviction_impacted_requests_total

Panel: Scheduler cache pressure
- runtime_scheduler_cache_pressure

Panel: “Starvation suspicion” (derived heuristic)
- High cache_pressure + high eviction in one tier + rising p99 for that tier

Speaker notes:
- This is where we validate the eviction-policy/scheduler contract.
- If we can’t tag victim_class in v1, we can still plot “evictions total” and add victim_class later.


Slide 11 — Panel mockup #5: “Allocation pressure + OOM risk”
Panel: Allocation failures (absolute) + rate
- increase(runtime_kv_alloc_failures_total[5m])

Panel: GPU memory used vs free (if we can split)
- gpu_mem_used_bytes, gpu_mem_free_bytes
- Optional: kv_cache_bytes_in_use vs non_kv_bytes (runtime instrumentation)

Panel: Near-OOM events / emergency behavior (if present)
- runtime_kv_emergency_evictions_total
- runtime_admission_control_rejections_total{reason=kv_pressure}

Speaker notes:
- Alloc failures are a paging-worthy symptom even if latency hasn’t spiked yet.
- Admission-control rejections show customer impact earlier than error rates.


Slide 12 — Table mockup: “Top offenders”
Table: Top pools by fragmentation (last 30m)
- columns: region, pool, model_family, traffic (tokens/s), fragmentation_ratio p50/p95, alloc_fail_rate

Table: Top routes/tenants by long-context mix
- columns: route/tenant, avg_context_len, context_len_p95, p99_decode_latency

Speaker notes:
- For Hosted, “route” is usually the best proxy; for Dedicated, “tenant/account”.


Slide 13 — Proposed alert set (summary)
Alert class A: “Hard symptoms” (page SRE oncall)
- Allocation failures > threshold
- Timeouts/error spike + kv symptoms

Alert class B: “Leading indicators” (ticket or slack notify; page if sustained)
- Fragmentation ratio sustained high
- Compaction thrash / budget exhaustion

Alert class C: “Canary regression” (blocks rollout)
- p99 regression in compaction-enabled pools relative to control
- alloc_fail_rate regression

Speaker notes:
- Avoid alert floods: we should page on symptoms, notify on indicators.
- Canary regression alerts can be more sensitive because blast radius is intentionally small.


Slide 14 — Alert proposal A1: Allocation failures
Name: KV allocation failures (critical)
Condition (per pool, per 5m window):
- increase(runtime_kv_alloc_failures_total[5m]) >= 1
AND
- traffic above minimal floor (to avoid false positives on idle pools)

Routing:
- page SRE oncall (hosted) OR dedicated oncall rotation for dedicated pools

Runbook link:
- eng-sre/runbooks/mitigating-kv-cache-fragmentation-incidents

Notes:
- This should page even if p99 hasn’t moved yet; alloc failures often precede timeouts.


Slide 15 — Alert proposal A2: Tail latency + kv correlation
Name: p99 decode latency spike with KV fragmentation high
Condition:
- p99_decode_latency_ms > SLO_threshold (pool-specific)
AND
- runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 (tunable)
For >= 10m

Action hints:
- If compaction_enabled=false: consider enabling compaction canary flag in that pool (if allowed) or increase eviction aggressiveness temporarily.
- If compaction_enabled=true: inspect budget utilization and compaction time per GiB; may need to reduce budget or adjust triggers.

Notes:
- The fragmentation threshold is initial; we will calibrate with baseline spreadsheet + perf suite.


Slide 16 — Alert proposal B1: Fragmentation sustained high (notify)
Name: KV fragmentation sustained high (warning)
Condition:
- runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio > 0.40 for 30m
AND
- alloc_fail_rate still low (so it’s early warning)

Routing:
- Slack notify #eng-runtime-oncall and #eng-sre (no page)

Notes:
- This is intended to catch slow-moving degradations or a single pool becoming pathological.


Slide 17 — Alert proposal B2: Compaction thrash / budget exhaustion
Name: Compaction budget exhausted frequently (warning)
Condition:
- runtime_kv_compaction_budget_utilization_ratio > 0.9
AND
- compaction_runs rate high (e.g., > N per minute)
For >= 15m

Interpretation:
- We are likely constantly compacting (possible trigger threshold too low)
- Risk: median latency regression due to sync/copies

Action:
- Reduce compaction budget, raise fragmentation trigger, or disable compaction in affected pool if median latency regresses.


Slide 18 — Alert proposal C1: Canary regression gate
Name: Compaction canary regression (block rollout)
Scope:
- pools where compaction_enabled=true AND rollout_phase in {canary, 25%}

Condition (relative):
- p99_decode_latency_ms in canary > p99_decode_latency_ms in control by > X% for 30m
OR
- alloc_fail_rate in canary > control by > Y (absolute)

Routing:
- notify #eng-releases, #eng-runtime, #eng-sre

Notes:
- Exact X/Y should align with perf-canary and release gating policy.


Slide 19 — “Bad pattern” example #1: Fragmentation creep → tail spike
Graph pattern:
- fragmentation_ratio slowly rises from ~0.15 → ~0.45 over 2–6h
- evictions increase gradually
- p50 latency stable
- p99 decode latency begins spiking during burst windows
- eventually alloc_failures appear (often at burst peak)

Interpretation:
- Fragmentation + bursty arrivals causes allocator search/rehash overhead and occasional reallocations.
- Mitigation: reduce fragmentation via compaction/eviction tuning; consider routing long-context away from this pool temporarily.


Slide 20 — “Bad pattern” example #2: Compaction thrash (median regression)
Graph pattern:
- fragmentation_ratio oscillates (sawtooth): rises → compaction event → drops → repeats frequently
- compaction_runs_total rate high; bytes moved high
- budget_utilization pinned near 1.0
- p50 decode latency increases 10–30% (even without big p99 change)

Interpretation:
- Compaction triggers too aggressive OR compaction cost too high on this hardware/model family.
- Mitigation: raise trigger threshold, cap budget lower, or change trigger mode (time-based → threshold-based).


Slide 21 — “Bad pattern” example #3: Eviction unfairness / tier impact
Graph pattern:
- overall eviction rate moderate
- p99 for latency_sensitive tier spikes, while best_effort stable
- scheduler_cache_pressure elevated
- if available: eviction victim_class shows unexpected evictions for latency_sensitive

Interpretation:
- Violation of scheduler contract; eviction policy may be selecting victims incorrectly under mixed loads.
- Mitigation: switch eviction mode to safer policy (v0), enable stronger pinning, or reduce multi-tenant mixing in affected pool.


Slide 22 — “Bad pattern” example #4: Allocation failures without fragmentation
Graph pattern:
- alloc_failures occur but fragmentation_ratio remains low
- gpu_mem_free_bytes trending down steadily
- long-context mix spikes

Interpretation:
- True memory pressure (not fragmentation). Likely workload shift (longer contexts, higher concurrency) or leak.
- Mitigation: admission control, reduce max context, re-route to higher-memory pool, investigate leak.


Slide 23 — Dashboard annotations we need (operational hygiene)
Annotation events to show on relevant panels:
- runtime config changes (compaction_enabled, budgets, trigger thresholds, eviction mode)
- rollout stage changes (canary → 25% → 100%)
- region/pool routing changes (SRE mitigations)
- runtime version deploy

Where annotations come from:
- release train events + config service audit log

Speaker notes:
- Half of “we can’t debug this” comes from not knowing what changed.


Slide 24 — Open questions / gaps (as of 2025-03-03)
1) Fragmentation ratio definition: confirm allocator-level formula; ensure stable across versions.
2) Can we tag evictions by victim_class in v1? If not, what surrogate can we use?
3) Do we have per-request attribution for “impacted_by_compaction” or “alloc_retry_count”? If yes, can we sample and expose it?
4) GPU memory accounting: can runtime expose kv_bytes_in_use reliably across model families?
5) Cardinality: define allowed label sets for hosted routes / dedicated tenants.

Owners:
- (1) Omar El-Sayed + Logan Wright
- (2) Sofia Ivanova + Allison Grant
- (3) Marcus Reed + Rina Kobayashi


Slide 25 — Next steps / delivery plan
- Align on metric schema + labels (ENG-2842)
- Build initial dashboard with core panels (ENG-2850)
- Add canary-specific panels/alerts (perf-canary PR + observability-pack PR)
- Run a 24h canary and tune thresholds using baseline results spreadsheet

Success criteria:
- Oncall can answer in <5 minutes: “Are tail lat spikes due to KV fragmentation/compaction?”
- Canary rollback decisions can be made based on explicit dashboard + alert signals

Contact:
- #eng-sre, #eng-runtime-oncall
- Owner: Allison Grant
